The settings seek reads from its configuration file and from its environment, generated from their JSON Schema definitions.

## seek configuration file

The JSON object seek reads from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/seek/config.json, or ~/.config/seek/config.json when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is empty or unset. Its keys are seek's variable names, and an environment variable with the same name takes precedence over the file. A Vault or OpenBao secret read through SEEK_VAULT_PATH holds fields with these same names. seek reads string values only and ignores other keys.

Definition: [configuration.file.schema.json](configuration.file.schema.json) (JSON Schema 2020-12). Type: object.

| Key | Type | Accepted values | Default | Example | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PARALLEL_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Parallel API key, used by `seek web parallel`, `seek research parallel` and `seek scrape parallel`. A seek server sends it to Parallel as the `x-api-key` header. |
| `EXA_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Exa API key, used by `seek web exa` and `seek scrape exa`. A seek server sends it to Exa as the `x-api-key` header. |
| `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Brave Search API key, used by `seek web brave search`. A seek server sends it to Brave as the `X-Subscription-Token` header. |
| `BRAVE_ANSWERS_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Brave Answers API key, used by `seek web brave answers`, `seek research brave` and the Brave planner of `seek research google --interactive`. A seek server sends it to Brave as the `X-Subscription-Token` header. |
| `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Perplexity API key, used by `seek web perplexity`, `seek research perplexity` and the Perplexity planner of `seek research google --interactive`. A seek server sends it to Perplexity as an `Authorization: Bearer` header. |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Google Gemini API key, used by `seek research google`. A seek server sends it to Google as the `x-goog-api-key` header. |
| `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Firecrawl API key, used by `seek scrape firecrawl`. A seek server sends it to Firecrawl as an `Authorization: Bearer` header. |
| `SEEK_SERVER_URL` | string (uri) | A URI |  | `https://seek.internal.example` | Base URL of a seek server. When it is set, the CLI sends every provider call to `<url>/v1/proxy/<upstream>` with the client token, and does not use local provider keys. The value is trimmed and trailing slashes are removed. |
| `SEEK_SERVER_TOKEN` | string |  |  |  | Client token for a seek server. The CLI sends the whole value as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, so a client's value is one token. `seek serve` accepts each entry of a comma-separated list, which allows rotation. |

Other keys: seek ignores keys it does not read.

## seek environment variables

The process environment seek reads, as an object of variable names and string values. An empty value counts as unset. Whitespace-only provider keys, SEEK_SERVER_TOKEN and Vault settings count as unset. Direct mode preserves nonblank provider key values as entered. The server trims provider keys before using them. The provider keys, SEEK_SERVER_URL and SEEK_SERVER_TOKEN are also configuration file keys; a set environment variable takes precedence over the file. The SEEK_VAULT_*, VAULT_* and BAO_* variables are read from the environment only.

Definition: [configuration.environment.schema.json](configuration.environment.schema.json) (JSON Schema 2020-12). Type: object; every value is a string.

| Key | Type | Accepted values | Default | Example | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PARALLEL_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Parallel API key, used by `seek web parallel`, `seek research parallel` and `seek scrape parallel`. A seek server sends it to Parallel as the `x-api-key` header. |
| `EXA_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Exa API key, used by `seek web exa` and `seek scrape exa`. A seek server sends it to Exa as the `x-api-key` header. |
| `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Brave Search API key, used by `seek web brave search`. A seek server sends it to Brave as the `X-Subscription-Token` header. |
| `BRAVE_ANSWERS_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Brave Answers API key, used by `seek web brave answers`, `seek research brave` and the Brave planner of `seek research google --interactive`. A seek server sends it to Brave as the `X-Subscription-Token` header. |
| `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Perplexity API key, used by `seek web perplexity`, `seek research perplexity` and the Perplexity planner of `seek research google --interactive`. A seek server sends it to Perplexity as an `Authorization: Bearer` header. |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Google Gemini API key, used by `seek research google`. A seek server sends it to Google as the `x-goog-api-key` header. |
| `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` | string |  |  |  | Firecrawl API key, used by `seek scrape firecrawl`. A seek server sends it to Firecrawl as an `Authorization: Bearer` header. |
| `SEEK_SERVER_URL` | string (uri) | A URI |  | `https://seek.internal.example` | Base URL of a seek server. When it is set, the CLI sends every provider call to `<url>/v1/proxy/<upstream>` with the client token, and does not use local provider keys. The value is trimmed and trailing slashes are removed. An environment value of only whitespace turns server mode off, even when the configuration file sets a URL. |
| `SEEK_SERVER_TOKEN` | string |  |  |  | Client token for a seek server. The CLI sends the whole value as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, so a client's value is one token. `seek serve` accepts each entry of a comma-separated list, which allows rotation. |
| `SEEK_SERVER_HOST` | string |  | `127.0.0.1` |  | Default for `seek serve --host`, the interface the server binds. The server image sets it to `0.0.0.0`. |
| `SEEK_SERVER_PORT` | string | Matches `^[0-9]+$` | `8787` |  | Default for `seek serve --port`, the port the server listens on, from 0 to 65535. |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | string |  |  |  | Base directory of the configuration file, which is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/seek/config.json`. When it is empty or unset, the file is `~/.config/seek/config.json`. The server image sets it to `/config`. |
| `SEEK_VAULT_PATH` | string |  |  | `seek`, `clients/my-seek-cli` | Path of the Vault or OpenBao KV secret within its mount, such as `seek`. Setting it turns Vault on: the server reads its secrets there, and a client in server mode reads SEEK_SERVER_TOKEN there when the environment does not set it. Leading and trailing slashes are removed. |
| `SEEK_VAULT_ADDR` | string (uri) | A URI |  | `https://vault.internal.example` | Vault or OpenBao address. It takes precedence over VAULT_ADDR and BAO_ADDR; one of the three is required when SEEK_VAULT_PATH is set. Trailing slashes are removed. |
| `VAULT_ADDR` | string (uri) | A URI |  |  | Vault address, used when SEEK_VAULT_ADDR is unset. It takes precedence over BAO_ADDR. |
| `BAO_ADDR` | string (uri) | A URI |  |  | OpenBao address, used when SEEK_VAULT_ADDR and VAULT_ADDR are unset. |
| `SEEK_VAULT_MOUNT` | string |  | `secret` |  | KV secrets engine mount. Leading and trailing slashes are removed. |
| `SEEK_VAULT_KV_VERSION` | string | `1`, `2` | `2` |  | KV secrets engine version. Version 2 reads `/v1/<mount>/data/<path>`; version 1 reads `/v1/<mount>/<path>`. |
| `SEEK_VAULT_REFRESH_SECONDS` | string | Matches `^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$` | `300` |  | How long seek uses the secret it read before it reads it again, as a non-negative number of seconds. A failed read after the first keeps the values already read. |
| `VAULT_NAMESPACE` | string |  |  |  | Vault namespace, sent as the `X-Vault-Namespace` header. It takes precedence over BAO_NAMESPACE. |
| `BAO_NAMESPACE` | string |  |  |  | OpenBao namespace, used when VAULT_NAMESPACE is unset. |
| `SEEK_VAULT_ROLE_ID` | string |  |  |  | AppRole role ID. When it is set, seek logs in with AppRole and needs SEEK_VAULT_SECRET_ID_FILE or SEEK_VAULT_SECRET_ID. AppRole takes precedence over a token file and a token. |
| `SEEK_VAULT_SECRET_ID_FILE` | string |  |  |  | Path of a file holding the AppRole secret ID, read once, when seek first configures its Vault client. It takes precedence over SEEK_VAULT_SECRET_ID. |
| `SEEK_VAULT_SECRET_ID` | string |  |  |  | AppRole secret ID, used when SEEK_VAULT_SECRET_ID_FILE is unset. |
| `SEEK_VAULT_APPROLE_MOUNT` | string |  | `approle` |  | Mount of the AppRole auth method. Leading and trailing slashes are removed. |
| `SEEK_VAULT_TOKEN_FILE` | string |  |  |  | Path of a file holding a Vault token, read again before each secret read so that a token rotated by Vault Agent is used. It applies when SEEK_VAULT_ROLE_ID is unset, and takes precedence over VAULT_TOKEN and BAO_TOKEN. |
| `VAULT_TOKEN` | string |  |  |  | Vault token, used when no AppRole role ID or token file is set. It takes precedence over BAO_TOKEN. |
| `BAO_TOKEN` | string |  |  |  | OpenBao token, used when no AppRole role ID, token file or VAULT_TOKEN is set. |
